objects.title: Erdős distinct subset sums problem (erdosproblems.com #1, $500)
objects.note: OPEN; 'cannot be resolved with a finite computation' (erdosproblems.com, fetched 2026-07-16). Computation informs the a(n) table, records, and constants — never the conjecture itself.

objects.title: A276661 — minimal largest element of an n-element sum-distinct set (the a(n) table)
objects.note: The program's primary ladder. Exact through a(10)=309 (VR-2).

objects.title: A005318 — Conway–Guy sequence u(n) (maxima of the CG sum-distinct sets)
objects.note: u(0)=0, u(1)=1, u(k+1)=2u(k)−u(k−round(sqrt(2k))). Generator: arms/conway_guy.py, calibrated against 14 published terms.

objects.title: Conway–Guy sets {u(n)−u(j) : j<n} — sum-distinct for all n (Bohman 1996)
objects.note: Sum-distinctness is a THEOREM (Bohman 1996), certificate-verified here only for n <= 30 (bitset ceiling). NOT optimal at n=12,13 (VR-2) — optimality of CG at general n is a refuted heuristic.

objects.title: a(10) — minimal max element, n=10
objects.note: Exact: 309 (Dyson, OEIS A276661, Oct 2025, published code; witness-verified in VR-3). The value VR-1 initially missed — see AUDIT-1/VR-2.

objects.title: a(11) — minimal max element, n=11 — THE LIVE FRONTIER
objects.note: OPEN window [462, 594]: lower binom(11,5) (DFX 2021), upper u(11)=594 (CG-11 witness, verified VR-3). Campaign: plans/P2_frontier_n11.md.

objects.title: a(12) — minimal max element, n=12
objects.note: Open; upper bound 1157 < u(12)=1164 — posted set certificate-verified here (VR-5); refutes CG-optimality at n=12. Window [924, 1157].

objects.title: a(13) — minimal max element, n=13
objects.note: Open; upper bound 2249 < u(13)=2284 — posted set certificate-verified here (VR-5). Window [1716, 2249].

objects.title: Dubroff–Fox–Xu lower bound: a(n) >= binom(n, floor(n/2))
objects.note: arXiv:2006.12988 (2021). The engine's own arms use only the weaker self-contained doubling bound for exhaustion floors; DFX is cited context (VR-1 §4).

objects.title: Bohman construction record: max element <= 0.22002·2^n asymptotically
objects.note: Bohman 1998, unbeaten since. Beating it at one n does NOT improve the asymptotic family record (VR-1 §5 claim-inflation guard).
